mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for two consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a fall in housing starts (HOUST) below 1700K signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% AND HOUST < 1700K in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods compared to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary inflation and tightening shock, which erodes real earnings and increases risk aversion, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month MA AND CPIAUCSL > 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from baseline during triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.5 percentage points month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which boosts wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a sharp demand contraction, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1.0% AND RSAFS monthly change < -1.0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between monthly industrial production (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns at a 5-day horizon: lower-than-expected industrial output predicts negative equity returns within the next week.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO surprises and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.
